scope: AS Pure Maths first school mock
finding: The existing mock subset covers 2D magnitude, vector addition, scalar multiplication and position-vector subtraction, plus the definitions of deduction, exhaustion and counterexample. It lacks dedicated short recall prompts for these 15 more specific vector/proof conventions. Coverage of original exam-question bank has NOT been exhaustively verified.

addedCards.front: For two non-zero vectors a and b, what algebraic relationship proves they are parallel?
To show distinct points A, B and C are collinear using AB and AC, what must you establish?
What is the position vector of the midpoint of A and B with position vectors a and b?
What is the distance AB in terms of position vectors a and b?
How do you obtain a unit vector in the direction of non-zero vector v?
A vector has magnitude r and direction θ from the positive x-axis. What are its components?
If the position vectors of A and B are a and b, what is BA?
If P divides AB internally in the ratio AP:PB = m:n, what is the position vector of P?
How can an even integer be written algebraically?
How can an odd integer be written algebraically?
How can an integer divisible by positive integer k be represented?
How can three consecutive integers be represented?
What makes a counterexample to a mathematical claim valid?
When proving a claim for all integers by deduction, how should n be chosen?

limits: No claim that AQA specification is fully covered
No claim that 2015-2026 AQA exam questions are all present
Any remaining difficulty applying vector geometry and proof belongs in worked exam questions
